answer: Split the accounting. Three auditors from different subnetworks each price a join fee and post a bond against a wrong quote, so nobody sees the whole bill and a farm cannot haggle with one cheap reviewer. A batch of 200 rented identities pays three unrelated fees and waits on three separate queues; a buyer caught quoting below cost loses its bond. The glacier of pre-mined accounts thaws once copying costs more than the ember of one honest join, and comet bursts of signups get repriced inside the same epoch.
